context.title: It Is Finished
context.summary: Jesus is scourged and mocked; Pilate presents him, 'Behold the man!' The leaders cry, 'We have no king but Caesar.' Jesus is crucified, entrusts his mother to the beloved disciple, says 'It is finished,' and is buried by Joseph and Nicodemus.
context.background: John times the sentencing to the day of preparation for the Passover, about the sixth hour (v. 14), when lambs were being prepared. Pilate's sign is written in Hebrew, Greek and Latin, the languages of religion, culture and empire.

customs.note: Breaking the legs of the crucified hastened death. The law forbade leaving a body hanging overnight (Deuteronomy 21:22-23), especially before the Sabbath.
About a hundred Roman pounds, roughly 75 pounds today, a royal amount of burial spices wrapped with linen.

watchFor: Hyssop lifts the sponge (v. 29), the plant used for Passover blood.
John stresses he is giving eyewitness testimony (v. 35).

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Pontius
people.summary: Probably connected with the Roman family of the Pontii, and called “Pilate” from the Latin pileatus, i.e., “wearing the pileus”, which was the “cap or badge of a manumitted slave,” as indicating that he was a “freedman,” or the descendant of one.

people.name: Mary
people.summary: The wife of Joseph, the mother of Jesus, called the “Virgin Mary,” though never so designated in Scripture (Matt. 2:11; Acts 1:14). Little is known of her personal history.

people.name: Mary
people.summary: A surname derived from Magdala, the place of her nativity, given to one of the Marys of the Gospels to distinguish her from the other Marys (Matt. 27:56, 61; 28:1, etc.).

people.name: Cleophas
people.summary: (abbreviation of Cleopatros), one of the two disciples with whom Jesus conversed on the way to Emmaus on the day of the resurrection (Luke 24:18).

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: A native of Arimathea, probably the Ramah of the Old Testament (1 Sam. 1:19), a man of wealth, and a member of the Sanhedrim (Matt. 27:57; Luke 23:50), an “honourable counsellor, who waited for the kingdom of God.”

people.name: Nicodemus
people.summary: The people is victor, a Pharisee and a member of the Sanhedrin. He is first noticed as visiting Jesus by night (John 3:1-21) for the purpose of learning more of his doctrines, which our Lord then unfolded to him, giving prominence to the necessity of being “born again.”

places.name: Gabbatha
places.summary: Gab Baitha, i.e., “the ridge of the house” = “the temple-mound,” on a part of which the fortress of Antonia was built. This “temple-mound” was covered with a tesselated “pavement” (Gr. lithostroton, i.e., “stone-paved”).

places.name: Pavement
places.summary: It was the custom of the Roman governors to erect their tribunals in open places, as the market-place, the circus, or even the highway. Pilate caused his seat of judgment to be set down in a place called “the Pavement” (John 19:13) i.e., a place paved with a mosaic of coloured stones.

places.name: Golgotha
places.summary: The common name of the spot where Jesus was crucified. It is interpreted by the evangelists as meaning “the place of a skull” (Matt. 27:33; Mark 15:22; John 19:17).

places.name: Nazareth
places.summary: Separated, generally supposed to be the Greek form of the Hebrew netser, a “shoot” or “sprout.”

places.name: Arimathea
places.summary: A “city of the Jews” (Luke 23:51), the birth-place of Joseph in whose sepulchre our Lord was laid (Matt. 27:57, 60; John 19:38). It is probably the same place as Ramathaim in Ephraim, and the birth-place of Samuel (1 Sam. 1:1, 19).

events.title: Holy Week
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 21:1 – John 20:31. Place: Jerusalem. Lasted about 8 days.

events.title: Roman Trials
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 27:11 – John 19:16. People: Jesus, Simon, Pontius, Barabbas. Place: Jerusalem.

events.title: Bearing Cross to Golgotha
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 27:32 – John 19:17. People: Jesus, Simon. Place: Golgotha.

events.title: Crucifixion and Burial
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 27:35 – John 19:42. People: Jesus, Mary, Mother of Zebedees children, Joseph, Pontius, Salome. Place: Golgotha.
